new_candidates.body:
## Summary

`GraspingManager.get_grasp_pose_at_index(index, in_world_frame=True)` raises `AttributeError: 'GraspingManager' object has no attribute 'object_path'` when the object prim is not on the stage. The docstring says it returns `None` in that case.

Both warning branches in that method build their message with `self.object_path`, which `GraspingManager` never sets (the attribute is `self._object_prim_path`). The "object prim not found" branch also uses `{e}`, which is not defined there. The `except` branch in `get_grasp_poses` uses `self.object_path` too.

`get_grasp_poses(in_world_frame=True)` handles the same "prim not found" case with a warning and `[]`, so only the per-index getter fails here.

Source: `source/extensions/isaacsim.replicator.grasping/isaacsim/replicator/grasping/grasping_manager.py`, `get_grasp_pose_at_index` and the `except` branch of `get_grasp_poses`.

## Steps to reproduce

In the Script Editor, on an empty stage:

```python
import omni.usd
from isaacsim.replicator.grasping.grasping_manager import GraspingManager
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

stage = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()
UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World/Object")

m = GraspingManager()
m.set_object_prim_path("/World/Object")
m.grasp_locations = [Gf.Vec3d(0, 0, 0.1)]
m.grasp_orientations = [Gf.Quatd(1, 0, 0, 0)]
print(m.get_grasp_pose_at_index(0, in_world_frame=True))  # pose

stage.RemovePrim("/World/Object")
print(m.get_grasp_poses(in_world_frame=True))              # [] with a warning
print(m.get_grasp_pose_at_index(0, in_world_frame=True))   # AttributeError
```

I ran this outside Kit, with `pxr` from `usd-core` and small stand-ins for `carb.log_warn` and `omni.usd.get_context()`, loading `grasping_manager.py` and `transform_utils.py` from `release/6.3` (9160c0e). Output, without the log lines:

```
(Gf.Vec3d(0.0, 0.0, 0.1), Gf.Quatd(1.0, Gf.Vec3d(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)))
[]
AttributeError: 'GraspingManager' object has no attribute 'object_path'
```

## Expected behavior

`get_grasp_pose_at_index` logs a warning and returns `None`, like `get_grasp_poses` does.

## How I found it

A lint pass flagged `e` as undefined in `get_grasp_pose_at_index`. Reading the method, I saw that `self.object_path` is not an attribute of the class either.

## Where this can show up

The grasping UI's evaluate step collects poses with `get_grasp_pose_at_index(i, in_world_frame=True)` and skips entries that are `None`. If the object prim was deleted or moved after the poses were generated, the step stops with the `AttributeError` instead of warning that some poses could not be retrieved. My estimate; I have not seen a field report.

## Environment

- `release/6.3` at 9160c0e, extension `isaacsim.replicator.grasping` 1.1.7
- Checked outside Kit on macOS arm64 with Python 3.11 and `usd-core`; I have not run Isaac Sim itself.

I have a small fix (use `self._object_prim_path` in the messages and drop the stray `{e}`) and can open a PR.
new_candidates.title: GraspingManager.get_grasp_pose_at_index raises AttributeError instead of returning None when the object prim is missing

new_candidates.body:
I found a position in the RoboCasa365 kitchen where the PandaOmron's `robot0_agentview_right` camera renders the window backdrop through an opaque wall. The robot reached this camera position during a rollout of `RecycleBottlesByType` in layout 44, style 22. I isolated the rendering behavior by resetting the same seeded environment and placing only the camera at the observed world pose.

## Versions

- RoboCasa 1.0.1, commit `a07e365c958c4216cd6bbd5f30b47f09a65c6f00`
- robosuite 1.5.2, commit `5ce6643f3092639d08f7b0f90ed1c6a84f50552c`
- MuJoCo 3.3.1, Python 3.11.17, NumPy 2.2.5
- EGL on NVIDIA H100, driver 580.178.04

## Reproduce

I ran the script below with the RoboCasa365 assets installed and `MUJOCO_GL=egl PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=egl python repro_wall.py`. It uses a fresh environment and then holds the camera pose fixed while changing the near plane. The pose is rounded to four decimal places from the rollout.

```python
import random

import numpy as np
from robocasa.wrappers.gym_wrapper import RoboCasaGymEnv

seed = 3396997499
random.seed(seed)
np.random.seed(seed)
gym = RoboCasaGymEnv(env_name="RecycleBottlesByType", split="pretrain", seed=seed, renderer="mujoco")
gym.reset()
env = gym.env
assert (env.layout_id, env.style_id) == (44, 22)
sim = env.sim
name = "robot0_agentview_right"
cid = sim.model.camera_name2id(name)
sim.data.cam_xpos[cid] = [5.2149, -4.8736, 1.75]
sim.data.cam_xmat[cid] = [0.6023, -0.4217, 0.6778, 0.7981, 0.3325, -0.5024, -0.0135, 0.8436, 0.5368]
for clip in (sim.model.vis.map.znear, 0.00002):
    sim.model.vis.map.znear = clip
    rgb = sim.render(width=256, height=256, camera_name=name)
    print(clip * sim.model.stat.extent, rgb.mean(), rgb.std(), rgb.min(), rgb.max())
gym.close()
```

## Expected

I expect the opaque wall to occlude the background in the agent view when the wall is directly in front of the camera.

## Actual

At the default effective near plane of 29.91 mm, the camera renders a nearly uniform gray frame. The camera's center ray intersects the wall backing about 3.2 mm from the lens. A shorter near plane of 0.60 mm exposes the wall at the same pose. The untouched reset image showed the kitchen normally.

| 256 × 256 RGB frame | Mean | Std | Min | Max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Default near plane at the wall | 163.885 | 0.337 | 162 | 164 |
| Short near plane at the same pose | 175.063 | 3.485 | 123 | 188 |

Could RoboCasa keep this camera far enough from the wall to preserve occlusion, or choose a smaller near plane for these kitchen scenes?
new_candidates.title: PandaOmron right agent-view camera clips through a kitchen wall at close range
